author: thsottiaux
text:
I have not checked, but Peter is probably in the top 10 users of Codex atm. Over 250B tokens in a few months is a lot. 

There is a new category of usage emerging where single individuals manage to leverage more intelligence solo compared to hundreds of other more casual users.

author: thsottiaux
text:
One last little present from the Codex team. Today we are launching our latest model: GPT-5.2-Codex-XMas.

It performs exactly the same as GPT-5.2-Codex, just with a needed personality upgrade for the season. Enjoy coding with Santa Codex!

$ codex -m gpt-5.2-codex-xmas https://t.co/WBEkHHhvJj

quoted.text:
For Codex users, to thank you all for the fun we've had over the last months, our first gift is that we have **reset rate limits and are lifting the usage limits to 2X the usual limits until the 1st of Jan**. Wish you all a merry holiday and lots of coding!!

Spread the word 👀 https://t.co/uKAZLhpp7r

author: thsottiaux
text:
GPT-5.2-Codex is out, further advancing our SoTA for professional software engineering and long-running agentic coding work.

It improves on instruction following, long-context understanding, and pushes the frontier including on cyber. 

$ codex -m gpt-5.2-codex https://t.co/rAc6oFInjx

author: thsottiaux
text:
We have added *experimental* support for skills and it combines well with GPT-5.2. Already seeing some cool things in the wild that leverage skills in codex. I think about skills as an extension of https://t.co/IG3o4GtOhd with progressive disclosure.

$ codex --enable skills

quoted.text:
codex + skills finetunes Qwen3-0.6B to +6 on humaneval and beats the base score on the first run.

I reran the experiment from this week, but used codex's new skills integration. Like claude code, codex consumes the full skill into context and doesn't start with failing runs. https://t.co/QyClw9qWyO

author: thsottiaux
text: @akmatori @sama @OpenAI yw, still in experimental phase right now!

author: thsottiaux
text: We have reset the usage limits for everyone in Codex, which helps us mitigate the issue the fastest and the team will continue to work on the underlying cause. This should propagate to all users over the next 10 mins, enjoy and apologies for the confusion!

quoted.text: We have discovered an issue in Codex that could lead to seeing inconsistent usage limits being displayed across Web, CLI and VS Code IDE. Team is working on fixing.

author: thsottiaux
text:
We have reset rate limits for all Codex users to compensate for the unusual high latencies in or near the US in the previous hours. Grateful for the team working hard behind the scenes to keep Codex running 24/7.

I do recommend trying out GPT-5.1-Codex-Max too if you haven’t!

quoted.text: Codex is back and operating at normal latency for users globally. The outage affected a significant part of our users who were in the US or routed to US clusters for processing. Team is making immediate improvements to help ensure Codex can run 24/7 in the future.

author: thsottiaux
text:
New model is out in Codex. Gets to same quality of solution faster and raises the ceiling for how complex of a tasks are achievable.

$ codex -m gpt-5.1-codex-max

Best experienced in the latest CLI version 0.59, which also packs a lot of other fixes and improvements. https://t.co/8UQUU7bl3l

author: thsottiaux
text: Imagine how unhobbled Codex will be once we rollout a proper fix to this. In the meantime, believe me, there are ... technical reasons for why this is. Not that I like them.

quoted.text:
This is even funnier. Codex will truncate any Bash/MCP tool output to 256 lines or 10kb. If the tool call outputs more than that, then the model only gets to see the first 128 lines, and the last 128 lines, but nothing in the middle.

Been like that since August. No wonder poor https://t.co/1kdkiraRjk

author: thsottiaux
text:
We've upgraded all our models in Codex. You can now use gpt-5.1, gpt-5.1-codex and gpt-5.1-codex-mini. 

All are a step-up that you should able to feel in daily use and you can expect us to continue pushing here on the frontier sooner than you might think. https://t.co/cnjU80h8gM

author: thsottiaux
text: @rafaelobitten @testingcatalog Decided to give Pro users priority processing instead, which feels better as hitting rate limits is almost not an issue for Pro users today

author: thsottiaux
text:
We gave gpt-5-codex a small sibling, you can now try gpt-5-codex-mini in Codex. Smaller, so up to 4X more usage included.

$ codex -m gpt-5-codex-mini

Also increased usage limits by 50% for Plus, Edu and Team plans and gave Pro priority processing for a faster experience.

author: thsottiaux
text:
More predictable usage in Codex. We landed optimizations behind the scenes that mean that you now will get the same usage throughout the day irrespective of the load or how traffic is routed. 

Before you could get unlucky and hit a few cache misses in a row and get less usage.

author: thsottiaux
text:
Small upgrade to Codex, we have updated gpt-5-codex within Codex.

The model should feel better, more collaborative, and across the board we gained a few percentage points for the evals we care about. Also a tad more token-efficient, needing ~3% less to achieve similar results.

quoted.text:
Is it me or Codex got a little smarter today? Same gpt-5-codex high on v0.55  but now it's more careful about edge cases and I don't have have to guide it too much.

GG! @thsottiaux @embirico

author: thsottiaux
text:
We promised unprecedented transparency for Codex and to take the reports of degradation seriously, despite seeing incredible growth week over week. 

Here is our report and what we have found over the last seven days
https://t.co/lJTCAeFHVQ

quoted.text:
We have concluded our initial investigation into increased reports of degradation for Codex and we will share it out by end of day. 

What is your bet on what we'll include in there and some of the findings?

author: thsottiaux
text: Codex had its strongest growth in one day yesterday since the launch of gpt-5-codex. Way to motivate the team during a gnarly investigation that's making us go through every piece of infra, hardware and line of code in our system.

author: thsottiaux
text:
On https://t.co/BuGVH2iy6F

While puzzling, we are taking this seriously and are in the middle of a full investigation started last Friday.

Current approach:
1) Upgrades to /feedback command
2) Reduce surface of things that could cause issues
3) Evals and qualitative checks

author: thsottiaux
text: Writing a lot of unmaintainable net new code is not the goal, saving time is. Codex pushes back on potentially bad ideas and compliments sparingly.

quoted.text: @thsottiaux Never seen an AI do this before: Codex refused my request and explained why doing it wasn’t a good idea. Made perfect sense. That’s why I ditched CC (plus the ridiculous usage limits). https://t.co/CwoaTEOfaH

author: thsottiaux
text:
We have reset everyone's limits for gpt-5-codex to allow you all to benefit more from it today and as a way to make up for the slowdowns earlier while we were provisioning additional GPUs. We'll continue to add capacity throughout the week to maintain the speed.

Enjoy!

author: thsottiaux
text:
With gpt-5-codex, some will feel that it's the best thing since sliced bread, some will see its quirks. 

Personally it is my favorite collaborator for coding, fast for small things, working hard when it matters and a solid jump in produced code quality.

$ codex -m gpt-5-codex
